- If sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent dip, true outcome often reverses or drops sharply — reduce forecast slope.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.00), model often underestimates downside risk — add 5–10% buffer for downward movement.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model tends to ignore it — adjust forecast to align with recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period volatility — increase sensitivity to last 5–7 days of history.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.20–0.33) followed by 0.00, model may overreact — dampen forecast growth after sentiment drop.
